candidate_records.name: Georgian Court
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010172 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Terraced two-bay four-storey house over raised basement, built c.1820. The NIAH describes a Flemish-bond yellow-brick façade, moulded granite plinth, rebuilt third floor, diminishing window openings, timber sliding sashes, later balconettes and steel guards, and a Roman Doric stone doorcase with triglyph-and-metope frieze. A five-storey rear building on Mabbot Lane spans the triple plot width across Nos.77-79; individual façades are expressed separately while sharing a roof. The appraisal identifies No.77 as part of the surviving early nineteenth-century Gardiner Street terrace.

candidate_records.name: City Manor
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010175 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Terraced two-bay four-storey house over raised basement, built c.1820. The NIAH records Flemish-bond yellow brick, moulded granite plinth, a Roman Doric doorcase, decorative wrought-iron balconettes, granite platform and approach, and spearheaded railings. The appraisal notes some alterations and poor condition of façade brickwork at survey time, while identifying the survival of historic form and features. A small mews building is set back from Mabbot Lane. Survey-time condition is not evidence of present condition.

candidate_records.research_notes: Terraced two-bay four-storey house over raised basement, built c.1820, with a three-storey rendered rear return. The NIAH records yellow Flemish-bond brick, chamfered granite plinth, replacement timber sliding sashes, a Roman Doric doorcase, granite platform and bull-nosed steps, and original wrought-iron railings. The original stone mews structure survives on Mabbot Lane but has altered façade, roof and interior. The appraisal notes the paired doorcase rhythm of Nos.74-80 and says the doorcase at No.81 belongs to the same broader architectural grouping, without claiming that the registrations form one object.

spatial_and_identity_cautions: Nos.77, 78 and 79 are three separately registered street-front houses. A later five-storey rear building on Mabbot Lane spans the triple plot width and shares a roof, while the NIAH describes the street façades individually. Do not create an extra archive object for the shared rear structure or merge the three registrations without independent footprint-level evidence.
No.80 is a separate registered house. Its mews building and the shared Georgian terrace context do not make it part of the triple-plot rear structure at Nos.77-79.
No.81 is a separate registered house. The appraisal describes paired doorcase patterns across a group of houses; this is an architectural relationship, not a merged building identity.
The queue's NAME field for 50010176 is blank. The evidence record preserves null rather than inventing a name.
Individual NIAH page coordinate pairs are preserved as raw values because the page does not label their CRS. Do not interpret them as EPSG:2157 or overwrite official CSV coordinates.
NIAH descriptions of use, condition and alterations are survey-time source statements, not present-day field verification.
No physical access, ownership, public access or current condition has been verified.
